title: g inside and outside a uniform Earth
caption: Gauss's law for gravity: inside a uniform sphere only the mass within r pulls, so g rises in a straight line from 0 at the centre to 9.8 m s⁻² at the surface (g = g₀r/R). Outside it falls as 1/r². At r = R/2 the field is half the surface value, 4.90 m s⁻².
alt: Graph of g against r/R: a straight line from zero at the centre up to 9.8 metres per second squared at the surface, then a curve falling as one over r squared. The point at half the radius is marked at 4.90.
description: The horizontal axis is distance from the centre in Earth radii (r/R); the vertical axis is g in m s⁻².
Inside (r < R) the enclosed mass grows as r³ and the surface area as r², so g = g₀(r/R): a straight line from 0 to 9.8.
Outside (r > R) all the mass counts as if at the centre, so g = g₀(R/r)²: 9.8 at r = R, 2.45 at r = 2R.
The example's point: at r = R/2, g = 4.90 m s⁻², half the surface value.
